## Subjective

58yo F, established patient with T2DM × 12 yrs, presents w/ progressive fatigue, polyuria, blurred vision × 3 weeks (location: systemic; quality: profound fatigue; severity: limiting ADLs; duration: 3 weeks; timing: progressive; associated symptoms: 9 lb weight loss, increased thirst). Denies chest pain, dyspnea, nausea/vomiting, focal neurologic symptoms. Recent A1c at outside lab 11.4% (up from 8.2% six months ago). PMH: T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, CKD stage 2. Compliant with metformin 1000mg BID, lisinopril, atorvastatin per report — but admits skipping noon dose of metformin "most days" due to GI upset. FHx: father T2DM, MI age 58. SHx: ex-smoker, no EtOH, sedentary.

## Objective

VS: BP 152/94, HR 96, RR 18, T 98.4°F, SpO2 98% RA, weight 196 lb (down 9 lb from 6 mo prior). Gen: tired-appearing, but no acute distress, no Kussmaul respirations. HEENT: dry mucous membranes; fundi w/ no acute changes. Cardiac: RRR no m/r/g. Lungs: CTAB. Abdomen: soft, NT. Extremities: no edema, distal pulses 2+. Neuro: alert, oriented, no focal deficits, monofilament intact bilaterally. Skin: no acute changes, no acanthosis. POC fingerstick glucose: 312 mg/dL.

## Assessment

1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemic crisis trajectory (E11.65) — A1c 11.4%, fingerstick 312, polyuria + weight loss over 3 weeks, at risk of progression to DKA / HHS without intensification
2. Hypertension, suboptimally controlled (I10)
3. CKD stage 2 (N18.2) — chronic, secondary to DM2/HTN
4. Hyperlipidemia (E78.5)

## Plan

Reviewed trends: A1c 7.9 (1 yr ago) → 8.2 (6 mo) → 11.4 (today) — clear progression. Decision: initiate basal insulin (glargine 10 units qHS, titrating per fasting glucose). Continue metformin (resolved GI upset by switching to ER formulation, taken once daily). Added empagliflozin 10mg daily for CV/renal benefit. UA today: trace ketones, no infection. BMP: Cr 1.3 (baseline), K 4.1, glucose 312. Lipid panel reviewed — at goal on atorvastatin. Counseled extensively re hypoglycemia awareness, sick-day management, when to call vs. ED. Diabetic educator referral placed. Glucometer prescribed, log review in 2 weeks. F/u 2 weeks for fingerstick log + insulin titration. Patient instructed to return immediately or call 911 for vomiting, AMS, fingerstick >400, or symptoms suggestive of DKA.

Decision against immediate hospitalization made jointly with patient given absence of acidosis, alertness, ability to tolerate PO, and reliable f/u. Documented decision-not-to-hospitalize as part of high-risk MDM.
